top_story: A month after Tehran threatened wider regional escalation in response to US warnings over its power grid and the Strait of Hormuz, violence in the occupied West Bank has sharpened a different but connected axis of instability centered on coercion, impunity, and civilian fear. On 22 April, Israeli settlers attacked a school area in the West Bank, killing two Palestinians including a 14-year-old boy, which reinforced an already worsening pattern in which children, schools, and first responders are exposed to direct settler violence. A parallel assessment published the same day indicates that sexual violence, threats, and harassment by settlers and Israeli soldiers are not episodic abuse but part of a broader pressure system driving Palestinian families from their communities, with women and children bearing the heaviest burden. The regional picture is therefore defined not only by state-to-state confrontation but by mounting localized violence that is steadily reshaping daily life, displacement, and the prospects for broader escalation.
